label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
Tolu, I'm in Biology 100L right now and I wanted Medicine. So this is me raising my hand lol. Your situation is literally my own story from last year, so let me tell you everything I know, the good and the not-so-good, because you asked for honesty and that's what you deserve.

**My own story first**

I wrote JAMB in 2025 and scored 251. I applied for Medicine and Surgery at a federal uni here in Lagos and they offered me Biology. The day I saw "Biology" on that portal, I locked myself in my cousin's room in Surulere and cried. I didn't eat that whole day. So when you said you've been crying since afternoon, I understand you well. It's not you being dramatic. You had your mind fixed on one thing and it felt like somebody just took it.

The family side was its own wahala. My mum was still telling people in church that I was doing Medicine for like two months after. I had to beg her to stop because people kept asking me questions and I didn't know what to say. So if you're also carrying your parents' expectations on top of your own disappointment, I understand that too.

**How Biology 100L actually is**

The courses we do in 100L are BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. I won't lie to you, physics and maths are the ones dealing with people. Many people come in thinking Biology is "just reading" and then PHY 101 and MTH 101 humble them. If you're strong in those two, you have an advantage already. If you're not, start preparing your mind.

Small money gist too: my lab coat was 6,500 naira, the dissecting kit was 9k, and the practical manual is extra on top. Just so you and your dad know what to plan for.

Now the part that surprised me. Our first BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted, I was fine. That day I realised I actually like this thing. I'm enjoying genetics and cell biology more than I ever expected. So to answer your question directly: no, Biology is not a bad course. A lot of the bad feeling around it is just because it's "not Medicine." When you remove that comparison, it's actually interesting. I didn't believe this when I was where you are now, so I don't expect you to fully believe me either, but it's true for me.

**The real gist about transfer**

This is the part everybody is shouting about without details, so let me give you what our level adviser told us. Please remember this is MY school. Yours can be different.

1. You need a CGPA of at least 4.5 out of 5 after 100L. And it's not just "4.5 and you're in." There must also be space in Medicine.
2. Our adviser said last year about 6 people got moved into Medicine from the whole faculty, and she thinks over 40 applied. So that's roughly 6 out of 40+. Transfer is real, but it's competitive.
3. She also said you need to have met the Medicine cut-off in both JAMB and post-UTME. I don't know your school's cut-offs or what you scored in post-UTME, so you have to check both. Your 268 is a good score, but 268 alone doesn't tell us whether you're eligible. It depends on what your school's Medicine cut-off is and how your post-UTME compares.

So about Kingsley saying transfer is a myth: that's not true. People do move. I've heard it directly from our adviser, with numbers. But favour saying "just read hard" is too simple. Reading hard is the minimum. You can read hard and still not get it if there's no space or if your post-UTME score didn't meet Medicine's cut-off from the beginning.

And since I'm being honest: my own CGPA after first semester is 4.31. Not 4.5. I'm still trying, second semester is still there, but I'm not where I need to be yet. I'm telling you this so you know it's not a "just enter and transfer" thing. It's hard. Nobody should accept Biology thinking transfer is automatic. That's the one thing I really want you to hear.

**On rewriting**

My secondary school classmate Ifeoma rejected a Pharmacy offer to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times since then and she's still at home. I'm not telling you this to scare you or say rewriting doesn't work, because people rewrite and get in every year. I'm telling you because staying at home is not as easy as people make it sound. Watching your mates go to school, reading the same JAMB syllabus again, the pressure from family. It's real.

But rewriting is not wrong either, if you're truly ready for it. 268 is a strong score. If you go back, prepare properly, and target a school or cut-off you can realistically beat, it can work. Just go into it with your eyes open, not because one person on a forum told you "one year is nothing." For some people one year is fine. For some it turns into two, three.

**What I'd actually do if I were you, before the deadline**

- Go to the faculty or the department in person and ask them the exact transfer rules for YOUR school. What CGPA do they need? Is there a quota? How many people got moved last year? Do you need to have met the Medicine cut-off in JAMB and post-UTME? Ask for the real answers from the people who handle it. Don't just trust forum people, and that includes me. My school's rules might not be your school's rules.
- Find out the Medicine cut-off for your school and compare it with your JAMB and post-UTME scores. That will tell you a lot about whether transfer is even possible for you.
- Be honest about physics and maths. If you can get a high CGPA with those courses in the mix, transfer is more realistic for you.
- Then ask yourself one quiet question: do I actually want Medicine, or do I want to be "a doctor" because that's what my parents and everybody around me expects? I had to ask myself this one too and it wasn't comfortable. There's no wrong answer, but your answer should guide your choice. If it's truly Medicine you want, then plan seriously for either transfer or rewrite. If part of it is the title and the pressure, then give yourself room to consider that Biology (or something you might move into later) could also be a good path for you.

**Last thing**

Whatever you choose, accept or rewrite, it's not the end of the world. I know it feels like it right now. A year ago I was crying in Surulere with no food, convinced my life had scattered. Now I'm in a lab cutting toads and actually enjoying genetics, still pushing my CGPA, still not sure where I'll end up, but I'm okay. You'll be okay too.

You're asking questions and trying to understand before you decide. That's already the right way to do it. Take a breath, go and get the real information from your school, talk to your dad and aunty with the facts in your hand, then decide.

If you want to ask me anything else about 100L, just reply here. I'll answer you. All the best Tolu 💛

— Amaka
